A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the presence of RPVO is a common finding after PE.
the presence of RPVO is associated with an increased risk of PE recurrence, chronic thromboembolism pulmonary hypertension and impaired exercise capacity.
the presence of RPVO is not a rare occurrence after acute PE and is a marker of a poor prognosis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
RPVO is not a simple imaging finding but rather an important clinical entity with a significant impact on patient's prognosis and quality of life.
RPVO is a common and underestimated complication after PE, and that its early detection is of paramount importance in terms of patient management.
V/Q lung scan should be performed early and after anticoagulant therapy to detect RPVO.
